name: test::test_case_basic_searched_forms::348

-- Test basic searched CASE (no base expression)
SELECT CASE 
  WHEN 1 = 1 THEN 'first'
  WHEN 2 = 2 THEN 'second'
  ELSE 'default'
END AS searched_case;

-- Test CASE with multiple conditions
SELECT 
  x,
  CASE 
    WHEN x < 0 THEN 'negative'
    WHEN x = 0 THEN 'zero'
    WHEN x > 0 THEN 'positive'
  END AS sign
FROM (VALUES (-5), (0), (7), (-2), (10)) AS t(x);

-- Test CASE with no ELSE clause (returns NULL for unmatched)
SELECT 
  x,
  CASE 
    WHEN x > 5 THEN 'big'
    WHEN x > 2 THEN 'medium'
  END AS category
FROM (VALUES (1), (3), (6), (10)) AS t(x);

-- Test CASE with NULL values in conditions
SELECT 
  x,
  CASE 
    WHEN x IS NULL THEN 'is null'
    WHEN x = 0 THEN 'is zero'
    ELSE 'has value'
  END AS null_check
FROM (VALUES (NULL), (0), (5), (NULL)) AS t(x);

name: test::test_case_nested_expressions::350

-- Test nested CASE expressions
SELECT 
  x, y,
  CASE 
    WHEN x > 0 THEN 
      CASE 
        WHEN y > 0 THEN 'both positive'
        WHEN y < 0 THEN 'x pos, y neg'
        ELSE 'x pos, y zero'
      END
    WHEN x < 0 THEN
      CASE 
        WHEN y > 0 THEN 'x neg, y pos'
        WHEN y < 0 THEN 'both negative'
        ELSE 'x neg, y zero'
      END
    ELSE 'x is zero'
  END AS classification
FROM (VALUES (5, 3), (-2, 4), (1, -1), (0, 5), (-3, -2)) AS t(x, y);

-- Deeply nested CASE

  val,
  CASE 
    WHEN val < 10 THEN 
      CASE 
        WHEN val < 5 THEN
          CASE 
            WHEN val < 2 THEN 'very small'
            ELSE 'small'
          END
        ELSE 'medium-small'
      END
    ELSE 'large'
  END AS size_category
FROM (VALUES (1), (3), (7), (15)) AS t(val);

name: test::test_case_in_select_where_groupby_orderby::351
stdin:
-- Test CASE in SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY
CREATE TEMP TABLE orders (id INTEGER, amount INTEGER, status VARCHAR);
INSERT INTO orders VALUES 
  (1, 100, 'pending'),
  (2, 250, 'completed'),
  (3, 50, 'pending'),
  (4, 300, 'completed'),
  (5, 75, 'cancelled'),
  (6, 400, 'completed');

-- CASE in WHERE clause
SELECT id, amount, status 
FROM orders 
WHERE CASE 
  WHEN status = 'completed' THEN amount > 200
  WHEN status = 'pending' THEN amount > 60
  ELSE FALSE
END
ORDER BY id;

-- CASE in GROUP BY clause
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN amount < 100 THEN 'small'
    WHEN amount < 300 THEN 'medium'
    ELSE 'large'
  END AS size_category,
  COUNT(*) AS count,
  SUM(amount) AS total
FROM orders
GROUP BY CASE 
  WHEN amount < 100 THEN 'small'
  WHEN amount < 300 THEN 'medium'
  ELSE 'large'
END
ORDER BY size_category;

-- CASE in ORDER BY clause
SELECT id, amount, status
FROM orders
ORDER BY CASE 
  WHEN status = 'completed' THEN 1
  WHEN status = 'pending' THEN 2
  WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 3
END, amount DESC;

-- Test CASE with aggregate functions
CREATE TEMP TABLE sales (id INTEGER, category VARCHAR, amount INTEGER);

  (1, 'electronics', 500),
  (2, 'clothing', 100),
  (3, 'electronics', 800),
  (4, 'food', 50),
  (5, 'clothing', 150),
  (6, 'electronics', 300);

-- CASE inside aggregate
SELECT 
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS total_sales,
  SUM(CASE WHEN amount > 200 THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS high_value_sum,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN amount > 200 THEN 1 END) AS high_value_count,
  AVG(CASE WHEN amount <= 200 THEN amount END) AS avg_low_value
FROM sales
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY category;

    WHEN category = 'clothing' THEN amount * 1.2
    ELSE amount
  END) AS weighted_total

name: test::test_case_in_having_and_with_window_functions::365
stdin:
-- Test CASE in HAVING clause
CREATE TEMP TABLE employees (dept VARCHAR, salary INTEGER);
INSERT INTO employees VALUES 
  ('Sales', 50000), ('Sales', 60000), ('Sales', 45000),
  ('IT', 70000), ('IT', 75000),
  ('HR', 55000), ('HR', 52000), ('HR', 58000);

SELECT 
  dept,
  AVG(salary) AS avg_salary,
  COUNT(*) AS emp_count
FROM employees
GROUP BY dept
HAVING CASE 
  WHEN dept = 'Sales' THEN AVG(salary) > 45000
  WHEN dept = 'IT' THEN AVG(salary) > 65000
  ELSE COUNT(*) >= 2
END
ORDER BY dept;

-- Test CASE with window functions
SELECT 
  dept,
  salary,
  CASE 
    WHEN ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) = 1 THEN 'highest'
    WHEN ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) = 2 THEN 'second'
    ELSE 'other'
  END AS rank_label
FROM employees
ORDER BY dept, salary DESC;
